On success, the scout remains unseen in the destination. On failure, the scout may check the foe Reaction table or fight one required solo round; foes have initiative for that first round and target the scout. Scout reactions resolve the same special outcomes as the main party where possible — including quest, blood offering, buy weapons, magic-item bribe, food/gem/item special bribes, sleep bonus, and scout-local gold bribes — using only gear and gold carried by the scout group. After that round the party can Rush to Scout to join the next combat round, or the scout can flee back toward the previous room. The scout cannot simply re-hide in the same location.

The party sheet separates Group 1 - Main Group from Group 2+ - Detached Group blocks, with each detached block labelled by its map element and reason. A Navigate button on detached group headings makes that group active for movement; detached scout rows also show Navigate back / Wait here controls. The Exits panel and map door markers then show routes from the detached group's tile instead of the main party's tile. The map highlights the active detached group with a distinct tile outline and marker.

When Wandering Monsters threaten a group left behind on another tile, the party sheet shows a Detached combat panel. Each click resolves one remote round for the heroes physically on that tile while the main party stays where it is; if the detached group falls, the monsters remain on that tile for the main party to face later.

Reactions, bribes, Trade Information, puzzle saves, flee/withdraw, spellcasting, common consumables, and class abilities use only heroes physically on the current map element. A detached hero away from the current room is visible on the party sheet but cannot use local actions until the party returns, and does not appear in combat — foe chips, hero chips, tactical room tokens, and combat hero rows show only combatants physically in the fight.

entries.title: Room Content
entries.summary: Entering a new map element rolls 2d6 on the Room Content Table.
entries.body:
When the party enters a newly generated room or corridor, roll 2d6 on the Room Content Table (p.106).

Results include empty rooms, vermin, minions, weird monsters, traps, special events, and treasure hoards.

Corridors use the corridor column where the table differs.

Living foes from this roll start combat immediately unless reactions or surprise rules apply.

entries.title: Backtracking
entries.summary: Moving to a visited tile may trigger a wandering-monster roll.
entries.body:
When the party moves to an already explored map element via a known connection, that is backtracking.

Roll d6 for wandering monsters on a 1 or 2 (see Wandering Monsters Table).

If wanderers spawn, they appear on the destination tile. Living foes there must be fought before resting or leaving.

Open doors and passages stay open when returning through them.

entries.title: Searching
entries.summary: Once per map element: roll d6 (corridors −1); on 5–6 choose one reward.
entries.body:
Search is attempted once per map element. Roll d6; in corridors subtract 1 from the roll.

On 5–6, the party finds something. After the successful roll, choose one reward:

• Hidden Treasure — gold or items using the Hidden Treasure rules.
• Secret Door — may reveal a new exit on this tile.
• Secret Passage — may shift the environment to caverns or fungal grottoes (EE p.112–113).
• Clue — choose the character who holds 1 Clue for puzzles, illusion doors, spells, trade information, and some quests.

Held Clues are spent deliberately after they are found. The Search Clue button gains a new character-held Clue; it does not spend held Clues.

entries.title: Clues
entries.summary: Gain Clues from Search; persistent character-held Clues can be traded or spent deliberately.
entries.body:
A successful Search reward choice can add 1 Clue to a selected character. Rulebook Clues accumulate across adventures; the app stores them on individual roster characters and restores the party total from those holders in the next dungeon. Legacy saves with pooled Clues are migrated to the first living character.

Uses:
• Reveal Secret — spend 3 Clues to reveal a selected Expanded Edition p.123 Secret; choose the PC who discovers it. Location of a Hidden Treasure is wired for an empty non-entrance room; Location of a Magic Item rolls magic treasure for the current room; Location of a Scroll grants a basic spell scroll; Weakness of a Foe gives +2 party Attack vs one chosen Major Foe for that combat; Deal with a Foe ends eligible non-vermin/non-Final-Boss encounters without treasure or XP; True Name of a Spiritual Entity offers angelic rescue/healing or demonic foe damage; New Spell adds a selected spell and one temporary slot for this adventure; Increase of Magical or Spiritual Power adds one permanent use of a selected spell/prayer; Your Enemy Is in the Dungeon swaps a Major Foe for a Chaos Champion and gives +1 Attack against it; The Prisoner adds an NPC rescue reward to a guarded room; Terrifying Secret forces the next eligible vermin/minion morale test to fail; Secret Diet spends 1 Food ration while camped outside for +1 Life this adventure; Bloodline of Dragon-Slayers is +1 Attack/Defense vs dragons; Recipe for a Potion validates 2 defeated Major Foes and 50gp components, then unlocks the 50gp Potion of Healing price in the equipment shop; Someone Will Pay Big Money for That triples one gem/jewel/jewelry sale and is consumed. Future-use Secrets show timing prompts on sheets, encounter-start hints in the log, and combat status reminders when the timing window opens.
• Someone Has Been Imprisoned (capture secret) — spend 3 Clues when a hero is held captive by foes to locate the captive hideout. A new 2d6×2d6 lair is generated adjacent to the current tile, guarded by the same foe type at double count. Captives are found there with d3 Life. Pay Level×10gp ransom instead of fighting if the foes' reaction allows. Available via the Reveal Secret picker (requires active captives) or the Find Hideout button in the Capture panel.
• Trade Information — on the p.102 reaction, gain 25gp per Clue held by heroes physically in the encounter without losing those Clues, and/or buy 1 Clue for 100gp using gold carried by heroes physically in the encounter.
• Spell learning — eligible wizard/elf expert spell learning may spend 3 Clues; Expert-trained L5+ druids may spend 3 Clues to learn an unlearned spell from the druid spell table.
• Illusion doors — spend 3 Clues instead of an illusionist spellcasting roll.
• Lever doors — spend 1 Clue or use a gnome gadget.
• Some quests and special discoveries (e.g. Kerrak Dar hoard: 1 Clue while Searching).

The app does not auto-convert every 3 Clues into a Secret/XP result; the player chooses the spend. Spending drains the selected/acting character's Clues first, then other holders if needed. Discovered Secrets appear on the home and active party sheets.

entries.title: Hidden Treasure
entries.summary: Search finds loot by formula; some hoards trigger alarms or traps.
entries.body:
When Search finds hidden treasure, roll gold and items using the Hidden Treasure Table (p.108).

Some results are protected by traps or alarms. An alarm may spawn wandering monsters before the party can claim the hoard.

Treasure already rolled on room entry (Treasure Table) is separate from hidden search results.

entries.title: Door Magic (Exploration)
entries.summary: Cast Fireball, Lightning, or Warp Wood on eligible doors outside combat.
entries.body:
In exploration, wizards (and others with slots) may cast door-targeting spells from the party sheet or exit panel:

• **Fireball / Lightning** — destroy iron doors when no foes remain in the room; shatter sealed doors per Door Table notes.
• **Warp Wood** — may ruin wooden doors or barriers.

Each spell cast consumes its once-per-adventure slot unless recovered by Rest.

Offensive door magic in combat follows normal combat spell rules.

entries.title: Iron, Sealed, Illusion, and Lever Doors
entries.summary: Some door results need spells, Clues, or class abilities instead of a simple open roll.
entries.body:
Door Table results beyond stuck/locked/trapped include:

• **Iron** — cannot be bashed; Rogue lock-pick or Fireball/Lightning only. Exits panel shows “no bash” and highlights spell destroy buttons when the party has no Rogue.
• **Sealed** — magical seal; spellcasting roll vs door level (once).
• **Illusion** — spend 3 character-held Clues or illusionist spellcasting roll.
• **Lever** — spend 1 character-held Clue or gnome gadget.

Unexplored doors show a hint that the first attempt rolls 2d6; warriors/barbarians get a Bash/roll-door action if the result is locked.

Fireball/Lightning on iron doors with no foes in the room destroys the door directly (no misleading “no targets” log).

entries.title: Lockpick and Bash
entries.summary: Locked doors: rogue lockpick (+Level), good lock-picks (+1), warrior/barbarian bash, crowbar (+1 bash for any class).
entries.body:
Locked doors cannot be opened by simply trying the handle.

• Rogues add +Level to lockpick attempts and always may try.
• **Good lock-picks** add +1 to lockpick attempts (any hero carrying them).
• Warriors and barbarians may bash instead of pick.
• A **crowbar** lets any class attempt a bash on locked or stuck doors and adds +1 to bash attempts.
• Other classes need magic, spells, or special tools unless the table says otherwise.

Encumbrance penalizes door attempts. Failed attempts may still trigger trapped doors.

entries.title: Opening Doors
entries.summary: Unexplored doors roll 2d6 on the Door Table; open doors stay synced both ways.
entries.body:
Closed doors must be opened before moving through. Roll 2d6 on the Door Table (p.109):

• Unlocked — opens easily.
• Stuck — Strength Save vs door level.
• Locked — Rogue lockpick or Warrior/Barbarian bash; encumbrance penalizes attempts.
• Trapped — triggers the Trap Table when opened or crossed.
• Iron, sealed, illusion, lever — special handling; spells, Clues, Fireball/Lightning, or Warp Wood may help in exploration.

Once a door is open, the linked exit on the other tile shows the same state.

Entrance threshold doors into the dungeon open without a roll the first time you explore through them (p.25). The outside dungeon exit starts open.

entries.title: Strength Saves
entries.summary: Stuck doors require a Strength Save vs door level.
entries.body:
Door Table results of Stuck require a Strength Save against the door's level.

Warriors and barbarians may bash stuck or locked doors instead of picking.

Encumbrance applies −1 to physical Saves including door attempts.

entries.title: Blade Poison
entries.summary: Apply poison to a weapon before combat; failed Saves inflict extra harm.
entries.body:
Blade poison is purchased from the wandering alchemist or found as loot.

Apply to a weapon before combat begins. On a successful hit, the foe Saves vs poison or suffers additional effects per table.

Poisonous foes may inflict lingering poison on heroes — repeated Saves until cured or duration ends.

entries.title: Holy Water
entries.summary: Throw at undead in combat or exploration; area effect per rulebook.
entries.body:
Holy water harms undead on a successful use. Throw in combat as an action or use in exploration when rules allow.

Barbarians may buy and use holy water despite not using other magic items.

entries.title: Illusion and Lever Doors
entries.summary: Spend held Clues or use door magic on special doors.
entries.body:
Illusion doors hide true exits until dispelled or bypassed with Clues, Fireball, Lightning, or Warp Wood.

Lever doors need the correct lever sequence — Clues from Search help.

Held Clues are owned by individual characters and spent deliberately; the Search Clue button gains a new character-held Clue, it does not spend them.

entries.title: Potions
entries.summary: Potion of Healing restores all lost Life once per hero per adventure.
entries.body:
Potion of Healing: restore all lost Life. Once per hero per adventure; usable even during combat as a free action.

Barbarians cannot use potions — they may carry potions for allies.

Buy from wandering alchemist or home equipment shop when available. Recipe for a Potion unlocks the 50gp equipment-shop price after its Secret prerequisites/payment are resolved.

entries.title: Scrolls
entries.summary: Burn to cast once; wizards may copy unknown spells into a spellbook (destroys scroll).
entries.body:
Any hero allowed scroll use may burn a scroll to cast the spell once (as L1 caster unless class says otherwise).

Wizards add +Level to scroll casting rolls.

Wizards may copy an unknown spell from a scroll into the spellbook — the scroll is destroyed. Copied spells become part of future preparation.

Barbarians cannot use scrolls.

entries.title: Charged Wands and Staves
entries.summary: Use charged wands and staves from inventory; Wand of Power adds +1 per declared charge for wizards.
entries.body:
Magical treasure may grant charged items such as Wand of Sleep (3 charges) or Fireball Staff (2 charges).

During combat or exploration, use the item button on the hero's party sheet. The spell resolves like a scroll cast (+Level for wizards, elves, druids, clerics, and illusionists) but does not consume a prepared spell slot.

Each use spends 1 charge. The inventory entry updates to show remaining charges; the item is removed when spent.

**Wand of Power (Fiendish Foes treasure):** Rolls 2d3 charges when found. Wizards only — before casting a memorized spell, declare how many charges to spend; each charge adds +1 to the spellcasting roll for that cast.

Offensive casts from magic items skip Reactions the same way as memorized offensive spells.

Barbarians cannot use magic items (may carry for allies).

entries.title: Caverns and Fungal Grottoes
entries.summary: Secret passage search can shift tables to cavern or fungal variants.
entries.body:
The party normally delves in the dungeon environment. Finding a secret passage via Search may move the party into caverns or fungal grottoes (EE p.112–113).

Each environment routes trap, treasure, special-event, and wandering tables to its variant where applicable.

Paper map mode limits placement to a 20×28 grid (p.149).

entries.title: Bags of Nails
entries.summary: 4gp each; one bag nails one door shut when resting.
entries.body:
Bag of nails costs 4gp from the equipment shop.

When Resting, spend one bag per door to nail shut. Nailed doors give warning if wanderers arrive during rest (party may strike first).

Rest without nailing lets wanderers surprise the party.

Only doors qualify — cavern openings cannot be nailed.

entries.title: Resting
entries.summary: Once per adventure in a cleared room with adjacent cleared tiles and nailable doors.
entries.body:
The party may rest once per adventure when all of the following are true:

• The party is in a cleared room (no living foes on the tile).
• Every adjacent explored room or corridor is also cleared.
• The room has doors that can be nailed shut (cavern openings do not qualify).

Each hero chooses to recover 1 Life or recover one spent ability (spell slot, Healing prayer use, rage attack, Luck point, or paladin prayer point). Heroes at full Life with nothing to recover gain nothing from a Life choice.

The party may nail doors shut using one bag of nails per door (4gp each). Nailed doors give warning on a wandering-monster roll (party may attack first). Unnailed doors let wanderers surprise the party.

After resting, roll d6 for wandering monsters on a 1.

Halflings may cook a Nourishing Meal once per adventure when resting: spend 1 Food ration per ally eating. Each eater heals +1 Life (in addition to rest recovery). Halflings also recover 1 Madness.

entries.title: Wandering Monsters
entries.summary: Roll d6 on 1 after rest, flee, noise events, or backtrack — category from table.
entries.body:
Wandering monsters use the Wandering Monsters Table.

Common triggers:
• After resting — d6 on 1.
• After fleeing combat — d6 on 1 may pursue.
• Backtrack movement — d6 on 1 or 2 (see table).
• Special events and alarms.

Nailed doors during rest give the party warning (party may attack first). Unnailed doors let wanderers surprise the party.

Corridor ambushes may target the rear guard and act before the party in round 1.

entries.title: Campaign Modes
entries.summary: Four campaign modes: Classical rolls, Slow and Sure completion, Old School tally, Slower Advancement bank.
entries.body:
Choose at adventure start (Campaign mode):

• Classical — earn XP rolls from minors, majors, secrets, and bosses; spend to advance mid-adventure.
• Slow and Sure — +1 Level for each hero who completes the adventure alive.
• Old School — tally XP from defeated foes and treasure; spend (Tier+2)×100 to level or buy a skill.
• Slower Advancement — bank XP like Classical, then spend Level XP (+ optional extra for +1) before rolling to advance.

Basic tier: advancement roll d6 > Level (6 always succeeds).
Expert-trained heroes: advancement roll d8+2 > Level or natural 7–8 on the d8. Expert-trained L5+ heroes may learn expert skills/spells instead of gaining a level.

Expert tier entry is a separate Tier training cost (500gp or 1 banked XP roll) and is required before Level 6, Expert dice, or Expert skill/spell learning.

Mid-adventure level-up: +1 Life and max Life, immediate class benefits, casters gain spell slots with in-session spell picker.

entries.title: Classical XP Rolls
entries.summary: Basic heroes roll d6 > Level; Expert-trained heroes roll d8+2 and may learn Expert skills instead of leveling.
entries.body:
Classical campaign mode: eligible heroes spend earned XP rolls mid-adventure.

Basic heroes roll d6 > current Level (6 always succeeds).
Expert-trained heroes roll d8+2 > current Level OR natural 7–8 on the d8 (Four Against the Abyss).

Expert-trained L5+ heroes may learn an expert skill/spell instead of gaining a level. Expert tier entry itself is separate: pay 500gp or 1 banked XP roll through Tier training first.

Spend pending rolls from the party sheet when ready. Same hero cannot level twice in one adventure.

Major foes and Final Boss grant extra rolls. Old School and Slower Advancement use tallies or banked XP instead.

entries.title: Old School and Slower Advancement
entries.summary: Bank XP from defeated foes; spend thresholds to level between adventures.
entries.body:
Old School XP: tally points from defeated enemies during the adventure. Between adventures, spend accumulated XP to buy levels per the Old School cost table.

Slower Advancement: similar bank with higher costs for a grittier campaign.

Slow and Sure: skip mid-adventure rolls — each survivor gains +1 Level when the adventure completes cleanly.

Choose the system when starting a session; it persists for that save.

entries.title: Level Advancement
entries.summary: Tier advancement roll mid-adventure; +Life, class perks, caster spell growth; Expert-trained heroes may learn Expert skills instead.
entries.body:
When an advancement roll succeeds during an adventure:

• Level up: +1 Life and +1 maximum Life (class Life offset applies).
• Class combat bonuses update immediately (+1/2 Level steps for half-level classes).
• Wizards gain L+2 total slots; elves L; druids 2+L; illusionists L+3 — pick new spells in session.
• Clerics gain improved Healing prayer (d6+L).

Basic tier uses d6. Trained higher tiers use the Forsaken Depths summary table (Expert d8+2, Heroic d10+4, Legendary d12+8, Epic d20+10).

After Expert tier training, Classical mode offers a fork on the party sheet: Level up or Learn expert skill/spell instead. Expert tier entry costs 500gp or 1 banked XP roll and is paid separately from the later skill-learning XP roll.

The same hero may not level twice in one adventure unless rules explicitly allow.

entries.title: Minor Encounter XP
entries.summary: Classical XP: one credit after every 10 minor-foe victories.
entries.body:
Under the Classical XP system, defeating vermin and minions (minor categories) counts toward a running tally.

Every 10 minor encounters cleared grants one XP roll credit for the party.

Major foes (weird, boss) grant immediate XP credits instead.

Progress persists on character records when you save, camp, or complete an adventure.

entries.title: Slow and Sure XP
entries.summary: +1 Level for each survivor who completes the adventure alive.
entries.body:
Choose Slow and Sure at adventure start.

When the party leaves the dungeon successfully, each surviving hero gains 1 Level automatically.

No d6 XP roll is required. Spell pickers appear if casters gain new slots.

entries.title: Attack Immediately vs Reactions
entries.summary: Skip Reaction roll only when charging in; offensive spells also skip Reactions.
entries.body:
At the start of combat you may Check Reactions or attack immediately.

Attack immediately: skip the Reaction roll and fight; eligible missile shots fire first in rooms.

Offensive spells (Fireball, Lightning, Sleep, etc.) cast at combat start also skip Reactions per p.146.

Defensive buffs (Protection, Barkskin, Illusionary Armor) do not count as attacking immediately — you may still Check Reactions first.

Surprised parties cannot attack first; foes act in round 0.

entries.title: Combat Initiative
entries.summary: Opening round order depends on surprise; corridors restrict who fights and who is hit.
entries.body:
Room combat: if the party is surprised or attacked immediately, eligible heroes with missile weapons fire once before melee. Otherwise party and foes alternate by phase.

Corridor combat: rear rank (#3–#4) fires missiles; front rank (#1–#2) melees; foes attack the front rank. Wandering ambushes in corridors hit the rear guard.

Surprised party: foes act first in the opening round.

Each combat round: party missiles (if allowed) → foe missiles/gaze → party melee → foe melee.

Offensive spells skip the optional Reaction roll (p.146). Defensive buffs may be cast before Check Reactions.

entries.title: Starting Combat
entries.summary: Room encounters wait for Start Combat; use Exits to leave without fighting.
entries.body:
When you enter a room with foes, combat does not begin until you choose Start Combat (wandering monsters and statue ambushes attack immediately).

While foes are present in exploration, use Exits to leave the room without fighting, or Start Combat when ready (p.146). The session UI shows a brief encounter hint listing foes on the tile.

After starting: Check Reactions (d6 on foe table) in the sticky action bar, Withdraw through a door in round 0, or Fight Round / an offensive spell to attack immediately.

The combat panel shows phase steps, foe cards, hero target/ability rows, round plan summary, and expected foe attacks. A top foe chip strip mirrors the bottom party chips: major foes are shown individually, identical vermin/minions are grouped, Final Boss chips are visually distinct, and hover/click details show traits such as undead, poison, MR, regeneration, and multiple attacks. Spells, potions, and class buttons remain on party sheets below.

Offensive spells cast at combat start skip Reactions. Defensive buffs do not.

Fight Round resolves the whole round — party attacks, then living foes.

entries.title: Surprise
entries.summary: Surprised parties cannot attack first; corridor wanderers may ambush the rear.
entries.body:
Some encounters surprise the party (wandering corridor ambush, certain events).

A surprised party cannot attack immediately in round 0 — Check Reactions or End Combat Round still applies, but foes may strike first.

Nailed doors during rest give warning so the party may attack first on a wandering roll.

Unnailed doors let wanderers surprise the party.

entries.title: Paper Map Mode
entries.summary: Optional 20×28 placement limit at session start (EE p.149).
entries.body:
When starting a session, choose Paper map mode to limit placement to a 20×28 grid.

Unlimited mode (default) uses a larger grid.

If no legal placement exists after truncation, the exit remains unexplored.

entries.title: Lady in White
entries.summary: Quest offer on eligible tiles; accept to track an Ongoing Quest.
entries.body:
The Lady in White may appear on map elements flagged by special content.

Accepting starts an Ongoing Quest tracked in the session panel with map markers.

Progress by reaching objectives, subduing or slaying targets, or returning items as the Quest Table specifies. The log uses Quest progress lines for accepted objectives, partial progress, completion milestones, and wrong-outcome boss defeats.

Claim Epic Rewards when the quest completes; the Ongoing Quests journal keeps the Claim button visible and explains why turn-in is blocked until the rules condition is met. The quest map marker opens the same objective/progress/turn-in summary and only enables Claim when the rules condition is already satisfied.

entries.title: Quests
entries.summary: Quest Table offers missions; subdue for bring-alive; Epic Rewards on claim.
entries.body:
Accept quests from the Lady in White or Quest Table events.

Track progress in Ongoing Quests. The journal shows objective, progress, turn-in, and Epic Reward claim state. Map markers show quest locations and the turn-in control explains current blockers such as missing gold, wrong tile, missing item, or incomplete boss objective.

Bring-alive objectives require subdual, not killing. If a Boss is slain instead, the quest remains pending and the log explains that a living captive is still needed.

Bring-head objectives roll and store a target Boss from a Boss Monster table. The next Boss encounter is matched to that target; only slaying that Boss acquires the head, and the head must be returned to the Quest-giver's tile before the Epic Reward can be claimed. If a Boss is subdued instead, the quest remains pending and the log explains that a slain Boss is still needed.

Slay-all requires the Final Boss defeated and all foes dead. On unlimited maps, the adventure must cover at least a 20x28 grid area before the claim can be made without returning to the Quest-giver.

Epic Rewards on claim may include expert spells, gear, or bonuses instead of standard treasure.

entries.title: Epic Rewards
entries.summary: Completing quests may grant Epic Rewards instead of standard treasure.
entries.body:
When a quest's objectives are met, Claim Reward on the Ongoing Quests panel.

Epic Rewards are rolled from the table. Book of Skalitos enters inventory as six basic wizard spell pages; each page may be burned like a scroll for Disperse Vermin, Blessing, Escape, Lightning, Fireball, or Sleep. The listed 650gp resale applies while unused. Gold of Kerrak Dar records a pending hoard reward; spend 1 held Clue while exploring to find 500gp, distributed with normal carry limits. Enchanted Weapon grants the receiving hero's weapon the table effect until adventure end: roll two attack dice and keep the better result. Shield of Warning is a permanent magic shield and its shield bonus still counts when ordinary shields are blocked by surprise from Wandering Monsters, fleeing, or shield-ignoring foes. Arrow of Slaying rolls a specific Major Foe target when awarded; a bow-using PC may consume it in combat to deal 3 automatic damage to that named target, then the arrow breaks. Holy Symbol of Healing adds +2 Life to a cleric's Healing prayer; if a fallen cleric's body and symbol reach the temple, the church pays for one resurrection attempt and keeps the symbol.

Bring-alive objectives require subdual and return to the Quest-giver with the living captive; bring-head requires the selected target Boss to be slain and its head returned to the Quest-giver's tile.

Permanent carried rewards persist to the character roster on clean dungeon exit; adventure-end effects such as Enchanted Weapon expire.

entries.title: Special Events
entries.summary: Room content and tables can spawn ghosts, merchants, quests, and environment events.
entries.body:
Special events come from room content rolls and dedicated special-event tables.

Examples in play:
• Ghost — interaction or combat per table.
• Wandering healer — once per adventure reroll on this tile.
• Wandering alchemist — buy potions or blade poison.
• Lady in White — may offer a quest.
• Caverns p.155 — trap, cavemen explorers, morlock spy, cave goblin scout, dwarf miner, or dwarf-party gem event.
• Fungal grottoes p.156 — trap plus rare item, cavemen, spore cloud, halfling scout, merchant, or mushroom-monk warning.

Event and feature table results log visible Event/Feature lines even in Summary mode. Effects that change a hero state or deal damage, such as ghost fear, fungal spore cloud, puzzle boxes, curses, healing, poison, or blessings, log targeted Effect lines naming the affected hero.

Ghost events log immunity, fear saves, failed fear saves (1 Madness via `resolve_fear_save` with `madness_source`; L1–4 may take 2 damage instead), and targeted Effect lines per hero. Repeat healer, alchemist, and refused Lady in White events log the substitution reason and route into the existing wandering-monster combat or Resolve Trap flow.

Statue and puzzle-box special features use explicit table choices: leave/touch the statue, or leave/attempt the puzzle box. Failed puzzle-box attempts deal 1 Life damage and leave the box available for another attempt. Pending statue/puzzle-box choices also show a distinct map marker; click it to focus the choice controls.

Caverns and fungal grottoes use their own special-event table variants. Cavemen, scout, dwarf miner, dwarf-party gem, fungal merchant, and mycelial-warning rows expose map-marker choices with hover hints and apply their PDF effects: feed/fight branches, paid no-surprise/+1 Save warnings, dwarf gem risk, dwarf miner next-tile preview after trade, merchant +20% equipment buys/resale, and the mushroom monk warning to ignore the next fungal Trap or Wandering Monsters encounter.

entries.title: Wandering Alchemist
entries.summary: Buy potions or blade poison when the alchemist special event appears.
entries.body:
The Wandering Alchemist sells Potion of Healing and blade poison during exploration when the event tile is active.

Purchases spend party gold from the buying hero's carried wealth (200gp dungeon cap).

Potions follow once-per-hero-per-adventure use rules. Blade poison is applied before a fight begins.

entries.title: Wandering Healer
entries.summary: Special event: once per adventure reroll on this tile for healing.
entries.body:
The Wandering Healer special event offers limited healing when encountered on a map element.

Each party may benefit once per adventure from the healer's reroll on that tile.

Treat as a special-event result from room content or the Special Events Table, not a guaranteed spawn.

entries.title: Claim Treasure
entries.summary: Split gold evenly among survivors; resolve traps before claiming protected hoards.
entries.body:
Claim Treasure on a cleared tile with a hoard divides gold evenly among living heroes (200gp carry cap each). If a hero is at the cap, their uncarried share is redistributed to living heroes with capacity; the log names capped heroes and the final payouts.

Items are assigned to carriers automatically where possible, and the log names each recipient.

Traps protecting treasure must be resolved first. Alarm traps may spawn wanderers before claim.

Empty treasure rolls remove the map marker.

entries.title: Treasure Rolls
entries.summary: Room entry rolls d6 on Treasure Table; claim splits gold among survivors.
entries.body:
Many rooms roll treasure when first entered (d6 on Treasure Table, p.157).

Empty hoards clear the treasure marker on the map.

Claim Treasure splits gold evenly among living heroes (respecting 200gp carry each), redistributes capped shares to heroes with capacity, and logs any +0gp capped heroes. Items are assigned with recipient names in the log.

Environment variants (caverns, fungal) use their treasure sub-tables where noted.

entries.title: Magical Treasure
entries.summary: Dungeon Magic Treasure grants wands, a teleport ring, Fool's Gold, a magic weapon, a healing potion, or a Fireball Staff.
entries.body:
Dungeon Magic Treasure Table (p.158): Wand of Sleep (3 charges), Ring of Teleportation, Fool's Gold, Magic Weapon, Potion of Healing, or Fireball Staff.

Use charged wands/staves from the party sheet; each cast spends 1 charge without using a memorized slot and follows the class limits printed in the table. Wand of Sleep is for wizards, illusionists, and elves. Fireball Staff is for wizards.

Magic Weapon rolls d6 for type when awarded: crushing light weapon, slashing light weapon, crushing hand weapon, slashing hand weapon, slashing two-handed weapon, or bow with 12 arrows.

Potion of Healing is a free action even in combat, heals all lost Life to one PC, and is limited to one potion per PC per adventure.

In fungal grottoes, row 6 on the Dungeon Magic Treasure Table rolls on the Rare Mushroom Table instead of awarding the Fireball Staff.

entries.title: Magic Weapons
entries.summary: +1 or +2 Attack when wielded; Fiendish +2 variant; class and magic restrictions apply.
entries.body:
Magic weapons from treasure grant +1 or +2 Attack when set as the hero's default wielded weapon.

Roll d6 when a generic magic weapon is found to determine weapon type (crushing/slashing light, hand, two-handed, or bow with arrows). Fiendish Foes may award +2 magic weapons.

Class restrictions and magic-use limits still apply for wielding/using the weapon, but treasure pickup may assign the weapon to any legal carrier with capacity when no current hero can wield it.

Resale: 100gp + 2× base weapon cost (p.19).

entries.title: Traps
entries.summary: Trapped exits roll on the Trap Table; rogues may attempt to disarm.
entries.body:
When the party finds a Trap, roll on the Trap Table (p.164) to determine its nature.

**Dungeon trap table (p.164):** Dart (random PC defense vs HCL+1), Poison Gas (all PCs poison save; barbarians/halflings +L), Trapdoor (lead save with armor/class mods), Bear Trap (lead save; Bear Trap Wound until healed), Spears (two random PCs defense vs HCL+4), Falling Stone (position 4 defense vs HCL+4; armor applies, shield does not; 2 damage).

**Caverns trap table (p.165):** Stalactite (random PC), Rockslide (all PCs; rogue/gnome/dwarf +L), Hidden Pit (lead save; trapped status; optional 1-Clue secret passage to **dungeon or fungal grottoes only**), Swinging Log (marching order until first fail; 2 Life), Toxic Mushrooms (mushroom-class immunity/lead skip; ranger/druid/outdoor forester +L; −1 Saves 6 rooms), Rolling Boulder (front/back; 1d3 marching order; block exit).

**Fungal grottoes trap table (p.166):** Sleep spores, spore cloud, slime patch, mycelium snare (player chooses lost held object), shrieking mushroom chance mods, cordyceps infection with undead boss rise.

A living rogue in marching-order position 1 or 2 may attempt to detect and disarm the trap before it goes off. If the disarm attempt fails, the trap triggers and the rogue still gets any Save allowed by the trap description.

Caverns **Miners' Amulet** on the lead hero negates one cavern trap per adventure.

Treasure protected by traps must be disarmed or resolved before claiming loot.

entries.title: Expert Skill Combat Actions
entries.summary: Declare round combat skills from the hero drawer; multi-target picks for Double Attack, Double Kick, Protective Incense.
entries.body:
Combat-round expert skills are chosen from each hero's Target/Ability rows in the Combat Focus hero drawer (or the legacy combat panel sidebar) before Fight Round:

• Whirlwind of Steel — once per encounter, chain up to two extra minion attacks at −1/−2 after a minion kill (no exploding dice).
• Double Attack — pick a primary and secondary foe before resolving.
• Deadly Strike, Dead Shot, Protective Incense — Protective Incense asks which ally receives the Defense bonus; Dead Shot rerolls the hero's next failed missile attack after declaration.
• Double Kick (acrobat) — choose up to two minor foes when declaring the trick.
• Knife Throwing — ranged light slashing weapon at −1; weapon returns after the fight.
• Continual Light — wizard or cleric forfeits attacks to maintain a worn light source.
• Turn Undead — once per encounter, affects all undead in combat; roll d6+½L vs each undead foe's Level, causing d6 Life loss on each success.

Reactive skills:
• Shield Bash — after an exploding Defense with a shield, free attack at −1 vs that foe (once per encounter).
• Dying Action — when reduced to 0 Life, one Attack at +1 before falling (once per encounter).

Combat Acrobatics swaps marching order (full turn, no attack). Turn Undead and sleep spores use party-sheet or hero-drawer buttons with hover text for eligibility/spent-use states.

Expert spells with extra targets: Infallible Missile (L8+) may pick a second foe; Phantasmal Binding and Water Jet use foe target rows.

entries.title: Combat Panel (Session UI)
entries.summary: Legacy sidebar combat panel when Combat Focus is off; spells and consumables also on party sheets.
entries.body:
When Combat Focus layout is inactive, the side panel shows a dedicated Combat section:

• Phase steps — Reactions, Plan round (or Bribe), Resolve.
• Foe cards — Life, level, tags, regen/poison/MR chips.
• Context notes — summoned beast, druid companion Life, corridor/ambush hints.
• Hero rows — marching order, plan label, Target and Ability selects (Bulwark Guard when sacrificing).
• Round plan — summary of each hero's target and declared ability before Fight Round.
• Expected foe attacks — preview of who each foe will strike (after reactions resolve).

During combat or a pending encounter, **Combat Focus** is the default layout (tactical map, command rail, hero drawer). See the Combat Focus reference entry.

Fight Round resolves the round and appends a one-line **Round summary** to the log. The summary names who damaged whom, which foe was killed by which hit when inferable, which hero took damage, regeneration blocks, or a clear no-event round.

Fight Round, Flee, Flee (Luck), and Withdraw buttons live here or on the slim combat deck. Withdraw offers a door picker when multiple exits exist.

Spells (with foe/ally targeting, Lifeforce amount, Mass Teleport allies/destination), potions, holy water, lantern oil, acid vials, and class ability buttons stay on expanded party sheets and the Combat Focus hero drawer.

entries.title: Map Exits Overlay
entries.summary: Collapsible Exits dock on the play map lists each exit with travel and door shortcuts.
entries.body:
The Exits overlay lists every **reachable** exit on the current room — only passages on visible, walkable map edges (same markers as the play map). Hidden or invalid exit rows are omitted.

Each row shows direction/kind and offers Travel or door shortcuts (Lock-pick, Bash, Open, Spellcast, Spend clues) with a hero dropdown when several characters can act.

**Iron doors:** status shows “no bash”; without a Rogue, Fireball/Lightning buttons are highlighted and sorted first.

**Unrolled doors:** note that the first attempt rolls 2d6; warriors see Bash/roll-door labels.

Long exit lists scroll inside the dock with a sticky scroll hint. Open/closed state persists in layout preferences.

entries.title: Session Map Layout
entries.summary: Play map zoom/pan, room panel, icon key, room-state markers, class icons, resizable splits, and saved layout prefs.
entries.body:
The session map supports viewport zoom and pan with overlays pinned to the viewport.

Collapsible panels: room details (top-right), Exits dock (bottom-right), icon key (bottom-left).

Room-state markers distinguish live foes, defeated foes, searched rooms, full/claimed/empty treasure, active/resolved traps, fallen heroes, detached heroes, active detached navigation groups, vendors, events, and quest givers. The current-party marker includes class icons for living party members.

During pending encounters and combat, a compact foe chip strip sits above the map/tactical stage while party chips sit below. Foe chips are color-coded by category, group identical minor foes, and make Final Boss status prominent.

Door and passage markers open the same navigation actions as the Exits panel, including scout-through when a scout is selected and detached-group movement when a detached group is active.

Draggable resizers adjust log height, map stage height, and side-panel width (double-click resets). Layout preferences persist in browser localStorage.

Paper map mode (optional 20×28 grid) blocks placement outside bounds at session start.

entries.title: Icon Registry and Map Markers
entries.summary: Rules tables and Icon Editor expose generated defaults plus icons.json overrides for map, class, and monster icons.
entries.body:
GET /api/rules/icons merges custom icons.json rows with generated defaults for room states, every playable class, monster categories, and each named monster.

The Home Rules tables panel lists those icon definitions under Icon registry (generated defaults + icons.json). The Icon Editor can assign user SVG/PNG/WebP files to any generated or custom row.

Unassigned icon rows use built-in CSS fallback glyphs. Existing icons.json entries override generated defaults, so committed custom art keeps priority.

The play map uses these definitions for room-state markers and the Icon Key. A single-monster-type room can use a monster-specific id such as monster-goblins; mixed groups fall back to the generic monster marker. A special event that resolves as wandering monsters uses the wandering-monsters marker instead of the generic event marker.

entries.title: Play Context (Environment + Terrain)
entries.summary: Two-axis context gates outdoor EE spells and ranger missile rules without a hex map.
entries.body:
The engine uses a minimal **PlayContext** (see `terrain.py` and home **play_context_table**) instead of a wilderness hex map.

**Environment** (session + tile): `dungeon`, `caverns`, or `fungal_grottoes` — routes trap, treasure, special-event, and magic-loot tables. Secret passages can switch environment.

**Terrain** (per tile): `indoor` (default), `outdoor`, `forest`, `swamp`, `jungle`, plus water/desert biomes for Water Jet modifiers. Random-dungeon entrance tiles are `outdoor` at the dungeon mouth. Imported adventures may set per-room terrain in the manifest.

**Session flags** (until rest): `alter_weather_active` from Alter Weather (−1 ranged, +1 Lightning Strike); `forest_pathway_active` from Forest Pathway.

**Wired checks:** druid Lightning Strike / Alter Weather / Entangle / Forest Pathway; illusionist Glamour Mask and Banquet; ranger double bow or sling outdoors; druid companion wilderness entry; mushroom hyphae wilderness routing.

Each session API response enriches `play_context` for the current map element. The live map panel shows terrain and active weather/pathway flags.

entries.title: Rules Tables Index
entries.summary: Home Rules tables are verified either as exact PDF rows, generated from locked PDF catalogs, or app validation tables.
entries.body:
The Home Rules tables panel is guarded by tests so every exposed table is explicitly classified for compliance. Tables either match exact rows from PDFs in Rules/, are generated from locked PDF-backed catalogs, or are app validation/help tables.

Exact/generated table keys currently exposed: abyss_boss_table, abyss_dragon_table, abyss_enchanted_banquet_table, abyss_magic_treasure_table, abyss_magical_defense_table, abyss_minions_table, entries.title: Adventure Lock (One Session Per Hero)
entries.summary: Heroes in an active dungeon session cannot join another until it completes or is deleted.
entries.body:
When a hero is assigned to an in-progress session, their roster entry shows they are gone adventuring and cannot be added to another party or start a duplicate session.

The lock clears when the session completes (clean exit) or is deleted from In Progress / Saved Games.

Camp outside and saved games keep the session open — regroup can swap heroes while the delve persists.

entries.title: Held Foes (Phantasmal Binding)
entries.summary: Held foes skip actions; attacks against them gain +2 and may subdue.
entries.body:
Phantasmal Binding and similar effects add a Held tag to a foe.

Held foes cannot act on their turn. Attacks against held targets gain +2 to hit and may apply subdual damage when subdual mode is active.

The combat UI shows held/poison/MR status on foe cards.

entries.title: Combat Focus (Tactical Layout)
entries.summary: Default combat layout: tactical room view, command rail (Exits/Encounter/Log), hero drawer, slim action deck.
entries.body:
When combat starts or foes are present on the tile, the session switches to **Combat Focus**:

• **Tactical map** — room-centric view with hero tokens and foe markers; optional **Cinema view** hides chrome for a larger map.
• **Foe chips** — top strip mirrors the party chips, groups identical minor foes, highlights Final Bosses, and exposes foe traits/tags/statuses on hover or click, including undead, poison, MR, caster, dragon, construct, regeneration, attacks, bloodied, subdued, and Final Boss.
• **Command rail** — Exits (travel/withdraw), Encounter (foe summary), and Log (Summary keeps outcome summaries and state/effect changes while Verbose shows rolls, table lookups, and math). When no higher-priority reaction/bribe/trade prompt is active, the status line summarizes active foe specials such as poison saves, MR tiers, regeneration, construct immunities, and multiple attacks. The encounter preview expands those live specials into short rules reminders, and expected foe attacks group multi-attack foes into one row with their target list and attack count.
• **Hero chips & drawer** — click a hero to open targeting, Ability picks (expert tricks + heroic Aggressive/Defensive Stance, Master Strike), class tricks, spells, potions, Halfling Luck rerolls, and status hover text such as Shield or +1 vs undead/demons without scrolling the main panel.
• **Slim combat deck** — primary round actions (Fight Round, flee, withdraw, reactions) stay on one row.

Multi-target planning (Double Attack second foe, Double Kick minors, Protective Incense ally, Infallible Missile L8+ second target) is declared in the hero drawer before Fight Round.

Layout fits one viewport on typical screens; exploration mode uses the standard session map layout.

entries.title: Class Tricks and Abilities (Tiers 2–4)
entries.summary: Tier 1–4 class tricks wired per home table; heroic/legendary 45/45 + 20/20 fully wired.
entries.body:
**Tier 1 (L1–4)** — rage, Luck, Panache, paladin prayer: fully wired. Paladin healing uses an explicit target selector on the party sheet.

**Tier 2 (wired):** acrobat tricks including Knife Throw; assassin hide; illusionist distract, Continual Light, Illusionary Knife Throw; gnome smokescreen/gadget/door/trap/free prisoner; mushroom spores; light gladiator dual wield/parry/counter; paladin steed (+1 mounted outdoors); swashbuckler dual wield + Panache. Targeted tricks show ally/foe selectors where needed.

**Tier 3–4 (wired):** Graceful Move, Hyphae (Search/Clue/secret door/passage), kukla prehensile hair lockpick + Army of Dolls, bulwark Sacrifice Defense/Shield + Limited healing, Divine Smite.

See **class_tricks_implementation_table** on the home Rules tables panel. The table describes targeted controls such as Combat Acrobatics ally swap, Lesser Necromancy fallen-hero target, and kukla ring/compartment choices. EE ability flags exposed by the shared expert/ability UI are listed separately in **ee_class_trick_flags_table**.

**Kukla rings and compartment:** wired. Green ring revives a selected fallen kukla, red ring poison targets a selected foe, and the torso compartment can stash/retrieve items or gold.

**Heroic & Legendary:** **45/45 heroic** and **20/20 legendary** wired.

entries.title: Map Fragment
entries.summary: Caverns treasure: once per adventure, preview the next unrevealed tile; 30gp gem bribe value in caverns.
entries.body:
A Map Fragment is found on the Caverns Special Item Table (p.160), not in the home shop.

During exploration in caverns, a hero with a fragment may use it from the party sheet. The fragment is consumed and the party may preview the next unrevealed exit tile before entering — once per adventure.

While in caverns, a Map Fragment counts as a gem for **Bribe** reactions and logs **30gp** counted value when surrendered.

The dwarf miner's trade information uses the same map-preview logic with different flavor text.

entries.title: Fiendish Foes (Optional Tables)
entries.summary: L3+ optional fiendish tables; mixed XP/treasure rules; wired boss/weird combat hooks and treasure routing.
entries.body:
**Session option (EE p.180):** `fiendish_foes_enabled` checkbox per adventure type (Random, Imported, AI-authored; default on). When enabled and **2+ heroes are L3+**, each vermin/minion/weird/boss table roll uses **d6** — 1–3 standard, 4–6 fiendish. Eligibility is checked at roll time (mid-adventure level-ups can activate Fiendish Foes). Traps, events, and special features still use the current environment tables.

**Mixed major + minor (p.180):** Defeating both together grants **2 XP rolls** (classical progression) and **suppresses minor treasure**; only major `treasure_rolls` apply (once per major foe name).

**Treasure after combat:** Sum each defeated foe type's explicit `treasure_rolls` once per name on the tile. `no_treasure` or a missing `treasure_rolls` field means **no roll**. Fiendish-tagged foes on the tile use `fiendish_foes_treasure_table` and `fiendish_foes_magic_treasure_table` (see home Rules tables).

**Lurking Mantlebeast (p.167):** Spot 2-in-6 (4-in-6 with rogue) on entry. **Turn Back** retreats through the entry passage without combat. **Start Combat** or a failed spot triggers the ceiling drop (L3 saves; pinned heroes cannot attack or flee and lose 1 Life/turn; success allows one attack without defending). Never a wandering monster.

**Fiendish Chaos Lord:** After victory, optional **Free Slaves** (+1 Clue, then Wandering Monsters roll) or **Decline**.

**Other wired hooks:** Skeletal Demon skeleton reinforcements; Hobgoblin Leader rattleblade; Doppelganger mimic/confusion; Acid Cube engulf; Giant Toad death-burst poison; Possessed Dwarf revival; Young Red Dragon fire breath; Stirge blood drain; random chaos lord powers; Chaos Slavers preset bear trap.

**Arrow of Slaying (p.163):** Rolls any major-foe table, then picks the target name from that table.

Home **combat_modifiers_table** and **play_context_table** rows document engine behavior. Tests: `tests/test_fiendish_foes_mode.py`, `tests/test_fiendish_foes_mixed_rules.py`, `tests/test_monster_combat_hooks.py`.

entries.title: Enchanted Paint
entries.summary: Fiendish treasure: create real gear (≤15gp list), rations, or doors; 1-in-6 runs out on use.
entries.body:
Enchanted Paint is awarded from Fiendish Foes magic treasure (not the home shop).

During exploration, use the party sheet to paint:

- Up to 8 Food rations
- Any non-magical shop item worth 15gp or less (no liquids) — pick from the paint list
- A door on a wall: creates an unlocked exit; connects to an adjacent tile if one aligns, or move through to roll a new map element as usual (EE p.186)

Roll d6 after each use — on 1 the paint runs out; otherwise it remains in inventory.

entries.title: Wand of Power
entries.summary: Fiendish treasure wand: wizard spends charges for +1 per charge on a spell cast.
entries.body:
Wand of Power is Fiendish Foes magic treasure. When found, roll 2d3 charges (minimum 1).

Wizards only. Before casting a memorized spell in combat, select how many charges to spend on the party sheet. Each charge adds +1 to the spellcasting roll for that cast and is removed from the wand.

Resale: 20gp per remaining charge.

entries.title: Hidden Pit — Climb Out & Secret Passage
entries.summary: Failed hidden pit Save traps the lead hero; rope or ally help climbs out; optional 1-Clue passage to dungeon or fungal grottoes.
entries.body:
When a **caverns** hidden pit trap triggers and the lead hero fails the Save, that hero gains **Trapped in pit** status and loses 1 Life.

From exploration, another living hero may help them climb out (**Climb out** on the party sheet), or the party may spend a rope from inventory so the trapped hero climbs alone.

If someone is trapped in the pit, the Clue panel offers **Find Secret Passage (1 Clue)**. Spending 1 held Clue reveals a secret passage to **Dungeon or Fungal Grottoes** (not Caverns). The clue option does not appear if the lead passes the pit Save.

See also **doors_traps** and **caverns_trap_table** on the home Rules tables panel.

entries.title: Hirelings (Abyss)
entries.summary: Expert-tier parties hire up to 2 retainers and 3 professional services per camp visit.
entries.body:
Four Against the Abyss pp.27–33. Requires at least one hero with **Expert tier training**.

**Camp outside:** the **Hirelings** panel handles hiring, dismiss, assign, treasure share, and resurrection. **Edit Party** (Camp panel) swaps roster heroes — separate from marching order.

**Marching order UI:** Main Group lists heroes and retainers in shared slots #1–#6. Acolytes, bodyguards, and spear carriers nest under their assigned hero and move with hero ↑/↓. Lantern bearers, porters, and other unassigned types appear as their own row with ↑/↓. When an assigned hero falls, surviving retainers test morale (d6 4+; 3+ with Commanding Presence); orphans show **Needs reassignment** until assigned to a living adjacent hero.

**Retainers** attack each combat round. Bodyguard intercept and acolyte Blessing preservation are optional player choices.

See **hirelings_table** on the home Rules tables panel.

entries.title: Alchemist Professional (Abyss)
entries.summary: Commission one potion per adventure: 50gp service fee plus material cost; brew completes when the party returns home.
entries.body:
Four Against the Abyss p.31–32. Expert tier required. Only **one alchemist order** at a time; counts as one of three professional services per camp visit.

**Commission at camp:** pay 50gp + material cost, choose potion and recipient hero. The pending brew resolves when the party **completes the adventure** (leaves the dungeon home).

**Completion roll:** automatic brews always succeed; others need d6 ≥ difficulty.

| Potion | Material | Roll | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Potion of Healing | 10gp | auto | Inventory item (standard healing potion rules) |
| Potion of Darksight | 15gp | 2+ | No −2 Attack/Defense without lantern light |
| Potion of Vigor | 10gp | 2+ | +1 saves vs poison/gas; Dark Plague immunity |
| Garlic Poultice | 1gp | auto | Blocks vampire level drain |
| Powdered Silver | 20gp | auto | +1 Defense vs werewolves |
| Elfblood Ointment | 35gp | 3+ | Immune to ghoul paralysis |
| Mindworth Extract | 60gp | 4+ | +2 Defense vs mind screamers; +2 saves vs tentacled brains |
| Elixir of Long Life | 1000gp | 5+ | On death: d6+L 6+ avoids death and heals 1d6 Life |

Failed rolls lose the brew (fee and materials are not refunded). See **hirelings_table** rows A1–A8 on the home Rules tables panel.

entries.title: Poison Expert (Professional)
entries.summary: Rogue L5+ pays 25gp to coat a slashing weapon or arrow; +1 vs first minion or boss level drop.
entries.body:
Four Against the Abyss p.32. Expert tier required. **25gp** professional service (counts toward 3/camp).

**Requirements:** hiring hero must be a **rogue Level 5+**. Only **one poison dose** at a time (no stacking with poison vials or vial envenom).

**Camp:** pay fee, then **Apply poison coating** to a slashing hand weapon or single arrow — item gains `(poisoned)` suffix.

**First attack with coated weapon:**
- vs **minion** (non-immune): **+1 Attack**, then coating wears off
- vs **boss** (non-immune): roll **d8 + L** vs monster level; on success **−1 level** with Life/attacks recalculated for the encounter (once per boss); coating wears off
- **Immune:** undead, dragons, elementals, golems — no modifier; coating still consumed on the attack

See **hirelings_table** Poison Expert row.

entries.title: Fear Saves and Madness
entries.summary: Any failed fear or terror save grants 1 Madness; L1–4 may take 2 damage instead.
entries.body:
Fear and terror saves use `resolve_fear_save` (paladin immunity, cleric +Level, Strong Will / Heroic Courage / Legendary Courage, halfling Yummy Meal bonus, Commanding Presence party bonus).

Any failed fear or terror save applies 1 Madness through the standard Madness pipeline (Strong Will ignores the first point; L1–4 heroes may choose 2 damage instead on the map panel).

**Note:** EE p.173 (Hoary Ogre battle cry) lists only the no-exploding-attacks penalty on a failed L4 Fear save — not Madness. The app applies both that penalty and Madness on failure per table-driven fear saves.

Druid companion death and other non-save sources still call `apply_madness_gain` directly.

entries.title: TCOTFD Playable Classes
entries.summary: Six TCOTFD classes with Courtship hooks: woo modifiers, saves, peaceful spell gate, hidden pathway, and Madness bonus.
entries.body:
**Wandering Alchemist (TCOTFD p.7-9)** — Life 3+L; saves as halfling; innate **Flower Portal once per adventure** (scroll reads unlimited — reader is not casting the class spell); re-roll Common/Uncommon ingredient harvest once; brew Apothecary Charts between Demesne encounters. **Expert L6+:** may learn **Surgeon**, **Herbalist**, or **Poison Expert** hireling training (1 XP each; free party services per 4AA rules; poison requires arsenic).

**Satyr (p.10-12)** — Life 7+L; +L Defense; +2×L Giving/Withholding; auto-fails mesmerize vs Maidens/Ladies/Matrons in the Demesne. **Outdoor pheromones:** eligible female humanoids only (medusa/she-orc/ogress/salamandrine oracle always female; vampire and others 1–3 on d6; whole group must qualify); d6+L vs foe level → seduce reaction and outdoor woo; pleased foes grant **treasure** (not Demesne gifts); failed Withholding outside Demesne costs **1 Life** not Melancholy; former lovers stay peaceful while the satyr remains. **Innate Blossoms spell** once per level (+L on roll, any Blossoms spell, no spellbook).

**Conservationist (p.13-14)** — Wizard variant L+3 slots; peaceful/Blossoms magic only; **forbidden offensive cast** (scroll or item) → **Curse of Tamas Zeya** (BoS entry 16, permanent loss). **Expert L6+:** may learn **Surgeon** or **Herbalist** (not Poison Expert).

**Halfling Lucky Wooers (p.31)** — spend Luck on failed Giving/Withholding rolls (Demesne woo panel checkbox).

**Demonologist (cross-book p.31)** — +½L Demesne wooing; +L on Blossoms scroll casts.

**Cambion / Succubus (BoS 14 & 49)** — hidden Riverside shortcut; +L Madness saves in queen's vault.

**Deferred:** Apothecary broad scope outside Demesne; wandering alchemist L1 expert skill list and halfling-skill expansion.

entries.body: When an adventure completes, the app records a campaign chronicle entry and creates structured guidance for closeout review. Supported TAG tasks still cite their specific TAG reference text, but this closeout workflow is app bookkeeping: review rewards, fallen or injured characters, XP markers, banking, storage, Guild finance, and other campaign consequences before starting another adventure.

entries.title: Campaign Chronicle
entries.summary: Persistent campaign history for completed adventures, TAG actions, closeout signoffs, and guidance updates.
entries.body: The Campaign Chronicle stores app-level history entries separately from active guidance. Completing, deferring, or dismissing guidance hides prompts from the active list but does not remove chronicle history. The dashboard shows recent chronicle entries in Guidance / Log and Campaign Management shows a longer campaign chronicle.

entries.title: Guidance Task Statuses
entries.summary: Structured guidance can be open, completed, deferred, or dismissed without deleting the chronicle.
entries.body: Guidance tasks are app prompts with priority and status. Open tasks appear in Needs Attention and Guidance / Log. Completed, deferred, and dismissed tasks leave active guidance but remain represented by campaign chronicle/log history. Use Complete for handled work, Defer for later campaign bookkeeping, and Dismiss only when the prompt does not apply.

entries.body: The modern Tables page includes tag_closeout_checklist_automation_table. It documents generated lead, route marker, XP, Guild, banking/storage, and guidance checklist checks plus their state sources and intended player actions.

entries.title: Campaign World Builder
entries.summary: App-owned campaign layer for grouping guilds, troupes, parties, characters, and settlements.
entries.body: Campaign Management is an app feature, not a printed TAG rule. The default campaign is Norindaal. New records default to Norindaal unless the creation form assigns another campaign. Each campaign can have one assigned guild; multiple troupes and settlements can belong to a campaign.

entries.title: Campaign Membership Boundaries
entries.summary: Characters belong to one party, one troupe, and one guild; parties belong to one troupe.
entries.body: The app enforces one current party, troupe, and guild per character. Parties are assigned to one troupe. If a character is assigned to a troupe that conflicts with their current party assignment, the app warns the user and the backend removes that character from the incompatible party.

entries.title: Friendly Settlements
entries.summary: Friendly towns, villages, and cities used for campaign ownership, services, travel, and home bases.
entries.body: Hearthmere is the default friendly settlement. Friendly settlements are campaign world records. TAG service and availability screens can use their names and size modifiers, but the campaign assignment itself is app bookkeeping rather than a printed TAG rule.

entries.title: Troublesome Towns Placeholder
entries.summary: Placeholder campaign records for future adventure-town supplements.
entries.body: Troublesome Towns are reserved for future Treacheries of the Troublesome Town Tome support. Current records are campaign placeholders only; no supplement-specific mechanics are claimed as implemented yet.

entries.title: Campaign Hex Map Placeholder
entries.summary: Planning placeholder for a future campaign/world hex-map editor.
entries.body: Campaign Management saves world-map planning notes now. The future hex-map editor should place settlements, track routes, and connect travel options to campaign geography without treating that app workflow as a printed TAG rule.

entries.title: Campaign Management Editing
entries.summary: Campaign Management supports inline editing, filtered lists, selected-campaign summaries, and safer delete warnings.
entries.body: Campaign Management is the app-owned world-builder layer. The dashboard lets the user search, sort, filter, create, edit, select, assign, and delete campaign records while keeping the default Norindaal, Adventurers Guild, Troupe1, and Hearthmere records protected. Delete prompts describe the records that will be unassigned or relinked.

entries.title: Campaign Assignment Integrity
entries.summary: Backend and dashboard safeguards keep campaign, guild, troupe, party, character, and settlement assignments consistent.
entries.body: The campaign world-builder release adds assignment-integrity checks across the app-owned campaign layer. A campaign may have one guild; guilds, troupes, friendly settlements, and troublesome-town placeholders each belong to one campaign. Troupes point to one guild and one friendly home settlement. Parties belong to one troupe and characters belong to one party, one troupe, and one guild. Moving a guild or troupe propagates campaign/guild context to affected parties and characters. Assigning a character to a conflicting troupe removes incompatible party membership and returns a guidance message. This is app bookkeeping, not a printed TAG rule.

entries.body: The modern Tables page includes campaign_worldbuilder_schema_table. It documents one guild per campaign, multiple troupes, multiple friendly settlements, troublesome-town placeholders, character assignment limits, and which defaults are protected by the app.

entries.title: Campaign Assignment Integrity Table
entries.summary: Tables exposes the campaign assignment limits, automatic updates, and user warnings.
entries.body: The modern Tables page includes campaign_assignment_integrity_table. It documents guild-to-campaign, troupe-to-campaign/guild/home, party-to-troupe, character-to-party/troupe/guild, and settlement-to-campaign assignment behavior.

entries.title: Modern Dashboard Management Polish
entries.summary: Troupe, Guild, Party, and Settlement Management share world context, filters, clearer assignment summaries, and detailed hover text.
entries.body: The modern dashboard management pages now start with a world-context panel, link back to Campaign Management, and expose searchable/filterable management lists. Troupe Management filters members and assigned parties. Guild Management filters Guild members and keeps Guild finance/closeout controls near the member list. Party Management filters saved parties and flags troupe assignment mismatches before resync. Settlement Management separates campaign settlement records from tracked TAG settlement state and distinguishes friendly settlements from troublesome-town placeholders.

entries.title: Modern Dashboard Management Table
entries.summary: Tables exposes a dashboard management workflow index for Troupe, Guild, Party, and Settlement pages.
entries.body: The modern Tables page includes modern_dashboard_management_table. It documents the primary controls, assignment model, hover-text focus, and rules-reference target for Troupe Management, Guild Management, Party Management, and Settlement Management.

entries.title: Party and Troupe Management
entries.summary: Saved parties belong to one troupe, and assigning a party syncs its members to that troupe context.
entries.body: Party Management is app bookkeeping for saved rosters. A saved party belongs to one troupe. The dashboard filters parties by name, member, and troupe, and shows assignment warnings when party members point to a different troupe. Assign Troupe updates the party and syncs the party characters to the selected troupe's campaign and guild context.

entries.title: Settlement Management Workflow
entries.summary: Settlement Management separates campaign settlement records from TAG tracked settlement state.
entries.body: Friendly settlements are campaign world records and can be home settlements for troupes. Troublesome towns are placeholders for later supplement support. The tracked TAG settlement list is the active downtime/service/travel state: selecting a settlement changes the current TAG settlement without travel, while Travel To logs travel and changes the current settlement. Size modifiers affect supported TAG availability checks.

entries.title: Character Management Deep Polish
entries.summary: Character Management exposes full roster sheets, readiness filters, weapon slots, armor/shield detection, and world context.
entries.body: Character Management now filters roster heroes by class, campaign, guild, troupe, party, and readiness warnings. Full sheets show core stats, campaign/guild/troupe/party/home settlement, Life readiness, weapon defaults, detected armor/shield inventory, carried inventory, spells, abilities, learned skills, traits, statuses, and reference links. Weapon slots use the existing roster weapon-defaults endpoint. Armor and shield are displayed from inventory rather than adding new persistent armor-slot fields.

entries.title: Go Adventure Setup Readiness
entries.summary: Go Adventure setup blocks critical start problems and surfaces review warnings before creating a session.
entries.body: Go Adventure now checks the selected party, adventure module, character state, world context, equipment warnings, and map cap before starting. Blocking issues include no party, not exactly four party members, fallen party members, active-session character locks, missing imported/AI module selection, and non-positive map caps. Injured members, equipment warnings, and campaign/guild/troupe context mismatches remain visible warnings for deliberate player signoff.

entries.title: Rules Artwork Registry
entries.summary: Local-only registry for licensed or personal-use artwork tied to rules references, tables, and dashboard pages.
entries.body: The app can show relevant art beside dashboard sections, rules reference entries, and tables through data/rules/artwork_registry.json. The configured asset paths point under assets/rules_art/local/, which is ignored by git. This means personal-use PDF crops or licensed images can appear locally without being pushed to GitHub.

entries.title: PDF Artwork Boundary
entries.summary: PDF artwork can be used locally through ignored assets, but extracted copyrighted art should not be committed unless publication rights are secured.
entries.body: Use tools/extract_rules_artwork.py to render a configured local artwork slot from an owned PDF. The generated image goes to assets/rules_art/local/ and is intentionally ignored by git. If you later obtain a publishing agreement, the same registry entries can point to approved committed assets or packaged licensed art.

entries.title: TAG Guidance and Adventure Closeout
entries.summary: Dashboard guidance summarizes unresolved TAG closeout work and recent campaign logs after adventures, Guild jobs, travel, banking, and settlement actions.
entries.body: Use the dashboard Guidance / Log section as an app checklist, not as replacement PDF text. After a TAG adventure completes, the app creates closeout tasks for supported obligations such as Guild loot share, upkeep, used availability reroll reset, leaving-restriction signoff, bank robbery recovery, hidden-trove risk/recovery, and pending TAG XP markers. The related Guild, Banking, Settlement, and Go Adventure pages expose the real controls that resolve many of those prompts. When a printed rule is not yet represented by a specific reference entry, the dashboard links to a targeted Rules Reference search and the owned PDF page rather than copying the rulebook text into the app.
